reason: /api/v1/health derived api_ready and status from SQL only (a promoted API row with a live lease), so a frozen or hung API worker was reported ready indefinitely and a killed one until the next 5 s reconciliation while every API call failed. Health now asks the promoted worker for its identity over the signed worker RPC (1 s timeout, 1 s cache) and reports api_state ready/not_responding/unavailable, with api_ready and status following it; static-asset routing keeps the SQL-only check (api_promoted). The UI keeps its memory-budget recovery screen for held admission only (api_state unavailable). The deployer's wait_ready() and wait_supervisor_host_ready() now also require one authenticated API read. The selection covers supervisor health and recovery (real promoted API worker frozen/killed), management, host knowledge bootstrap health, deployer readiness waits, the UI health mapping and both recovery-screen suites.
exclusions: test_runtime_management.py::test_owned_project_refuses_real_shutdown_without_notifying_launcher is left out: it fails identically on pristine main (dd1c200) after the recent shutdown/ledger merges (it expects state 'uncertain', the ledger now records 'failed'); the rest of that file is selected by name. test_runtime_host_knowledge_bootstrap.py::test_production_serve_runtime_syncs_owned_product_collection_on_lan is left out: it requires a non-loopback LAN address and fails identically on pristine main here; the rest of that file is selected by name. ui/src/api/client.test.ts is not selected because three of its existing cases (mission and harness mutation mapping) already fail on main; the new health-mapping cases live in ui/src/api/clientHealth.test.ts. PostgreSQL variants run where NEBULA_TEST_POSTGRES_URL is set; the selection passed locally on SQLite and PostgreSQL 16. No native or Playwright cases: the UI's visible behaviour is unchanged (the recovery screen still follows held admission); real-Core frozen/killed API evidence and the local deployer read are recorded in the PR. The deployer was never run against a remote host.
